questions.question: The term of office of the Attorney General of India is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Not fixed by the constitution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 76** of the **Indian Constitution** establishes the office of the **Attorney General of India** (AGI), who serves as the highest law officer in the country.
 
• The **Constitution of India** does not provide a fixed **tenure** or **term of office** (such as 5 or 6 years) for the Attorney General.
 
• The AGI is appointed by the **President of India** and holds office during the **pleasure of the President**, which means they can be removed at any time without a specific process.
 
• There are no specific **grounds for removal** mentioned in the Constitution for the AGI, unlike the procedure for judges of the **Supreme Court**.
 
• Conventionally, the Attorney General resigns when the **Council of Ministers** (the Government) resigns or is replaced, as the appointment is made based on the advice of the **Union Cabinet**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Qualifications and Appointment**:

 
 
• To be appointed as AGI, a person must be qualified to be appointed as a **Judge of the Supreme Court**.
 
• This requires being a **Citizen of India** and having served as a **High Court Judge** for at least 5 years or as an **Advocate of a High Court** for 10 years.
 
 
 
• **Functions and Rights**:
 
 
• The AGI provides **legal advice** to the **Government of India** on matters referred by the President.
 
• Under **Article 88**, the AGI has the right to speak and participate in the proceedings of both **Houses of Parliament** (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) but does **not have the right to vote**.
 
• They have the **right of audience** in all courts across the territory of India while performing official duties.
 
 
 
• **Remuneration**:
 
 
• The **remuneration** of the AGI is not fixed by the Constitution; it is determined by the **President of India**.

questions.question: On which festival day of Rongali Bihu do people traditionally visit relatives and exchange gifts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kutum Bihu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rongali Bihu**, also known as **Bohag Bihu**, is the most prominent festival celebrated in **Assam**, marking the beginning of the **Assamese New Year** and the arrival of the spring season.
 
• The festival spans seven days, known as **Xaat Bihu**, and is deeply rooted in the agrarian culture of the state, celebrating the onset of the seeding time.
 
• **Kutum Bihu** is traditionally observed as the **third day** of the festival sequence. The term **Kutum** in the Assamese language signifies **relatives** or **kinfolk**.
 
• On this day, people focus on maintaining social ties by visiting the homes of their **extended families**, **in-laws**, and **close friends**.
 
• The core tradition involves the exchange of **gifts** and hosting elaborate meals, where traditional delicacies like **Jolpan**, **Pitha**, and **Laroo** are served to guests.
 
• This phase of the festival serves to strengthen **communal harmony** and familial bonds after the personal and spiritual rituals of the preceding days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Goru Bihu**:

 
 
• Observed on the last day of the outgoing year (Sankranti), it is dedicated to the **worship of cattle**.
 
• Cows are washed with **Maha-Haladhi** (turmeric and black gram) and stroked with sprigs of **Dighaloti** and **Makhioti** plants for protection.
 
 
 
• **Manuh Bihu**:
 
 
• The first day of the **New Year**, where people take ceremonial baths and seek blessings from **elders**.
 
• It is characterized by the presentation of the **Bihuwan** (the traditional **Gamosa**) as a token of high esteem and affection.
 
 
 
• **Bohagi Bihu**:
 
 
• This is a general nomenclature for the entire spring festival, often used interchangeably with **Rongali Bihu** to denote the month-long festivities of **dance** and **folk music**.

questions.question: The small intestine receives digestive secretions from which two organs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liver and pancreas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **small intestine**, specifically the **duodenum**, is the primary site for the chemical digestion of food. It receives vital digestive juices from two major accessory glands: the **liver** and the **pancreas**.
 
• The **liver** secretes **bile juice**, which reaches the duodenum through the **common bile duct**. Bile contains no enzymes but is essential for the **emulsification of fats**, breaking down large fat globules into smaller micelles to increase the surface area for enzyme action.
 
• The **pancreas** functions as a major secretory organ that produces **pancreatic juice**. This juice contains crucial enzymes such as **trypsinogen**, **chymotrypsinogen**, **amylases**, **lipases**, and **nucleases**, which are necessary for digesting proteins, carbohydrates, and fats.
 
• Both the bile duct and the pancreatic duct join together to form the **common hepatopancreatic duct**, which opens into the duodenum, guarded by the **sphincter of Oddi**.
 
• The secretions from these organs are highly alkaline, helping to neutralize the acidic **chyme** received from the stomach, creating an optimal **pH (around 7.8)** for intestinal enzymes to function.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liver**

 
 
• It is the **largest gland** in the human body, weighing approximately **1.2 to 1.5 kg** in an adult.
 
• Beyond digestion, it performs functions like **detoxification**, **protein synthesis**, and the storage of **glycogen**, **Vitamin A**, and **Vitamin D**.
 
 
 
• **Pancreas**
 
 
• It is a **heterocrine gland**, meaning it has both exocrine functions (secreting digestive enzymes) and endocrine functions (secreting hormones like **insulin** and **glucagon**).
 
• The endocrine part consists of the **Islets of Langerhans**, which regulate blood sugar levels.
 
 
 
• **Excluded Organs**
 
 
• **Kidneys**: Part of the **urinary system**, responsible for filtering blood and removing nitrogenous wastes like **urea**.
 
• **Spleen**: A lymphatic organ that acts as a reservoir for **erythrocytes** (RBCs) and filters the blood for the immune system.
 
• **Lungs**: Central organs of the **respiratory system** designed for the exchange of **oxygen** and **carbon dioxide**.

questions.question: Which Prime Minister is the only one to have received both India's Bharat Ratna and Pakistan's Nishan-e-Pakistan awards?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Morarji Desai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Morarji Desai** served as the **4th Prime Minister of India** from **1977 to 1979**, leading the first **non-Congress government** under the **Janata Party** banner.
 
• He is the only Indian citizen to have been conferred with the highest civilian awards of both India and Pakistan: the **Bharat Ratna** and the **Nishan-e-Pakistan**.
 
• In **1990**, the Government of Pakistan honored him with the **Nishan-e-Pakistan** for his significant efforts in fostering peace and improving diplomatic ties between the two South Asian nations.
 
• The Government of India awarded him the **Bharat Ratna** in **1991**, recognizing his immense contribution to Indian politics and his role as a freedom fighter and administrator.
 
• His tenure as Prime Minister was marked by the dismantling of the restrictive structures imposed during the **Emergency (1975−1977)** and a commitment to **Gandhian principles** and fiscal discipline.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**:

 
 
• A founding member of the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**, he served three terms as Prime Minister and received the **Bharat Ratna** in **2015**.
 
• He is credited with making India a nuclear power through the **Pokhran-II** tests in **1998**.
 
 
 
• **Lal Bahadur Shastri**:
 
 
• The **2nd Prime Minister of India** who led the country during the **1965 Indo-Pakistani War** and popularized the slogan **Jai Jawan Jai Kisan**.
 
• He was the first person to be posthumously awarded the **Bharat Ratna** in **1966**.
 
 
 
• **P. V. Narasimha Rao**:
 
 
• Served as the **9th Prime Minister** and is celebrated for implementing the **1991 Economic Reforms** (LPG model) that transformed the Indian economy.
 
 
 
• **Financial Milestone**: **Morarji Desai** holds the record for presenting **ten Union Budgets**, the highest number by any Indian Finance Minister in history.

questions.question: The Tehri Dam is located on which river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhagirathi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tehri Dam** is a multi-purpose rock and earth-fill embankment dam located on the **Bhagirathi River** near **Tehri** in the state of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• Standing at a height of **260.5 meters** (855 feet), it is the **highest dam in India** and ranks among the tallest dams in the world.
 
• The dam serves as the primary component of the **Tehri Hydropower Complex**, which includes the **Tehri Dam & Hydroelectric Project** (1,000 MW) and the **Koteshwar Hydroelectric Project**.
 
• The reservoir created by the dam, known as **Tehri Lake**, has a surface area of approximately **52 square kilometers** and provides water for irrigation to **270,000 hectares** of land.
 
• The project also supplies significant amounts of **drinking water** to the urban populations of **Delhi** and **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• Construction of the dam officially began in **1978** with financial and technical assistance from the **USSR**, and the first unit was commissioned in **2006**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Yamuna River**:

 
 
• It is the longest tributary of the **Ganga** and originates from the **Yamunotri Glacier** in the **Bandarpunch peaks**.
 
• Significant structures include the **Lakhwar Dam** and the **Dakpathar Barrage**.
 
 
 
• **Ganga River**:
 
 
• The **Bhagirathi** is considered the source stream of the **Ganga**, which officially takes the name **Ganga** after meeting the **Alaknanda** at **Devprayag**.
 
• The **Farakka Barrage** is a major structure located on this river in **West Bengal**.
 
 
 
• **Godavari River**:
 
 
• Known as the **Dakshin Ganga**, it is the largest river system in **Peninsular India**.
 
• Key projects include the **Jayakwadi Dam** in **Maharashtra** and the **Sriram Sagar Project** in **Telangana**.

questions.question: The first Indian to win a Grand Slam title was Mahesh Bhupathi. In which year did he achieve this feat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1997**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahesh Bhupathi** etched his name in history by becoming the **first Indian** to win a **Grand Slam title** in **1997**.
 
• He achieved this historic feat in the **Mixed Doubles** category at the **French Open** (Roland Garros) held in **Paris**.
 
• Bhupathi partnered with Japanese player **Rika Hiraki** to clinch the title, defeating the top-seeded American pair of **Patrick Galbraith** and **Lisa Raymond** in the final with a score of 6-4, 6-1.
 
• This victory was a landmark moment for **Indian Tennis**, as it broke the barrier for Indian athletes on the global professional circuit.
 
• Following this success, he reached the **World No. 1** ranking in doubles in **1999**, further solidifying his status as a legendary sportsman.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahesh Bhupathi**:

 
 
• Born on **June 7, 1974**, in **Chennai**, he is one of the most decorated doubles players with a total of **12 Grand Slam titles**.
 
• He won **4 Men's Doubles** titles and **8 Mixed Doubles** titles throughout his career.
 
• He is famous for his partnership with **Leander Paes**, known as the **'Indian Express'**, together winning three Grand Slam titles and reaching the finals of all four majors in **1999**.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Shri** in **2001** and the **Arjuna Award** in **1995** for his contributions to sports.
 
 
 
• **Grand Slam Context**:
 
 
• The **French Open** is the only Grand Slam tournament played on **clay courts**, known for its slow surface and high bounce.
 
• The other three Grand Slam events are the **Australian Open** (Hard court), **Wimbledon** (Grass court), and the **US Open** (Hard court).
 
• Bhupathi's success paved the way for other Indian stars like **Sania Mirza**, who became the first Indian woman to win a Grand Slam title in **2009**.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a component of xylem tissue in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Companion cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Xylem** is a complex permanent tissue in vascular plants primarily responsible for the **conduction of water and minerals** from the roots to the aerial parts of the plant.
 
• The xylem tissue is composed of four distinct types of cells: **Tracheids**, **Vessels** (or tracheae), **Xylem parenchyma**, and **Xylem fibers**.
 
• **Tracheids** and **Vessels** are the main water-conducting elements; they are dead at maturity and possess thick, **lignified cell walls** to withstand high internal pressure.
 
• **Xylem parenchyma** is the only **living component** of the xylem tissue, primarily functioning in the storage of food materials (starch) and the lateral conduction of water.
 
• **Companion cells** are specialized **parenchymatous cells** that are thin-walled and contain dense cytoplasm and a prominent nucleus.
 
• Unlike the components of the xylem, **Companion cells** are fundamentally associated with **Sieve tube elements** within the **Phloem** tissue, which is responsible for the translocation of organic nutrients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phloem Tissue Components**:

 
 
• **Sieve Tubes**: Long, tube-like structures that lack a nucleus at maturity and transport **photosynthates**.
 
• **Companion Cells**: Regulate the metabolic activities of sieve tubes and help maintain the **pressure gradient** required for nutrient transport.
 
• **Phloem Parenchyma**: Living cells that store resins, latex, and mucilage.
 
• **Phloem Fibers**: Also known as **bast fibers**, these are dead sclerenchymatous cells providing mechanical strength.
 
 
 
• **Functional Differences**:
 
 
• **Xylem transport** is generally **unidirectional** (upward movement).
 
• **Phloem transport** is **bidirectional**, moving sugars from leaves (source) to storage organs or growing parts (sink).

questions.question: Which BIMSTEC Summit led to the decision to establish the Secretariat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Third Summit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Third BIMSTEC Summit** was held in **Nay Pyi Taw, Myanmar**, on **March 4, 2014**, where the heads of state decided to provide a permanent physical structure to the organization.
 
• The leaders signed the **Memorandum of Association (MoA)** on the establishment of the **BIMSTEC Secretariat** during this summit to enhance institutional capacity and coordination.
 
• Following this decision, the **BIMSTEC Secretariat** was formally inaugurated in **Dhaka, Bangladesh**, on **September 13, 2014**.
 
• The establishment of the **Secretariat** marked a shift from a purely consultative mechanism to a more structured **inter-governmental organization** with a dedicated budget and staff.
 
• The **Secretariat** is responsible for facilitating the implementation of projects, managing the **BIMSTEC** calendar, and supporting various technical and ministerial meetings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **First Summit**:

 
 
• Held in **Bangkok, Thailand**, in **2004**, it was the inaugural summit that upgraded the grouping from ministerial to summit level.
 
• It focused on establishing the **Framework Agreement** on the **BIMSTEC Free Trade Area (FTA)**.
 
 
 
• **Second Summit**:
 
 
• Conducted in **New Delhi, India**, in **2008**, focusing on poverty alleviation and regional connectivity.
 
• It emphasized cooperation in the fields of **energy security** and **counter-terrorism**.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Summit**:
 
 
• Organized in **Kathmandu, Nepal**, in **2018**, with the theme **Towards a Peaceful, Prosperous and Sustainable Bay of Bengal Region**.
 
• It resulted in the signing of the **Memorandum of Understanding** on the **BIMSTEC Grid Interconnection**.
 
 
 
• **BIMSTEC Overview**:
 
 
• Founded in **1997** through the **Bangkok Declaration**, it comprises seven members: **Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka, and Thailand**.
 
• **Sumith Nakandala** from **Sri Lanka** served as the first **Secretary General** of the permanent **Secretariat**.

questions.question: India's women's kabaddi team won its first Asian Games gold in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2010**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Women's Kabaddi** discipline was officially introduced as a competitive event for the first time in the **Asian Games** during the **16th edition** held in **Guangzhou, China**, in **2010**.
 
• The **Indian Women's Team** scripted history by clinching the **first-ever gold medal** in the sport, defeating **Thailand** in the final with a score of **28−14**.
 
• This victory established India's absolute dominance in **Kabaddi** on the continental stage, as both the **Men's** and **Women's** teams secured **Gold Medals** in the same year.
 
• The team was spearheaded by prominent players like **Mamtha Poojary**, who played a significant role in India's gold-winning campaigns in both **2010** and the subsequent **2014 Incheon Games**.
 
• Prior to the **2010** debut, **Kabaddi** was predominantly a male-dominated sport in international multi-sport events, making this **gold medal** a landmark moment for **women's sports in India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chronology of Kabaddi in Asian Games**:

 
 
• **Men's Kabaddi**: It was introduced much earlier as a medal sport at the **1990 Beijing Asian Games**, where India won the inaugural gold.
 
• **2014 Edition**: India successfully defended its title at **Incheon, South Korea**, by defeating **Iran** in a closely contested final.
 
• **2018 Edition**: At the **Jakarta-Palembang Games**, the Indian women's team's winning streak ended as they settled for the **Silver Medal** after losing to **Iran**.
 
• **2022 Edition**: Held in **Hangzhou (in 2023)**, India regained the **Gold Medal** by defeating **Chinese Taipei**.
 
 
 
• **Governing Bodies and Rules**:
 
 
• The **Amateur Kabaddi Federation of India (AKFI)** is the national body that governs the sport, while the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)** manages it globally.
 
• For women's international matches, the **court dimensions** are **12 meters × 8 meters**, and the match duration consists of **two halves of 15 minutes** each.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: The Law of Octaves was applicable only up to which of the following elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1866**, the English scientist **John Newlands** arranged the then-known **56 elements** in increasing order of their **atomic masses**.
 
• He observed that the chemical and physical properties of every **eighth element** were a repetition of the properties of the **first element**, similar to the notes in a musical octave.
 
• This classification, known as **Newlands Law of Octaves**, was found to be applicable and valid only up to **Calcium** (atomic number 20).
 
• For elements heavier than **Calcium**, the periodicity of properties broke down, as every eighth element no longer matched the properties of the first element in the vertical column.
 
• The law worked well only with **lighter elements** and failed to account for the transitional behavior of heavier elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Limitations of Newlands Law**:

 
 
• **Limited Scope**: Newlands assumed only **56 elements** existed in nature and that no more would be discovered, which was later proven wrong.
 
• **Incorrect Grouping**: In an attempt to fit elements into his table, he placed dissimilar elements like **Cobalt** and **Nickel** in the same column as halogens like **Fluorine** and **Chlorine**.
 
• **Noble Gases**: The discovery of **Noble Gases** (He, Ne, Ar) later made the law irrelevant because the eighth element was no longer the one with similar properties.
 
 
 
• **Thorium**:
 
 
• It was the **56th** and final element in Newlands periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen**:
 
 
• It was the first element in the arrangement due to its lowest **atomic mass**.
 
 
 
• **Potassium**:
 
 
• While **Potassium** is an alkali metal that follows the octave rule relative to **Sodium**, the overall systematic application of the law ceased immediately after **Calcium**.

questions.question: Who is credited as the architect of India's Green Revolution and was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M. S. Swaminathan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M. S. Swaminathan** (1925–2023) was a renowned **agronomist** and **geneticist** who is widely celebrated as the **Father of the Green Revolution in India**.
 
• He was posthumously conferred with the **Bharat Ratna**, India’s highest civilian honor, in **2024** for his transformative role in ensuring **food security** for the nation.
 
• During the 1960s, he spearheaded the introduction of **High-Yielding Varieties (HYV)** of wheat and rice, which dramatically increased agricultural productivity and helped India overcome the **ship-to-mouth** crisis.
 
• He served as the Director General of the **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)** and later the **International Rice Research Institute (IRRI)**, contributing extensively to agricultural research and policy.
 
• Swaminathan also headed the **National Commission on Farmers** (2004), where he proposed the **Swaminathan Formula** for determining the **Minimum Support Price (MSP)** at 50 percent above the cost of production (C2 + 50%).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Verghese Kurien**:

 
 
• Known as the **Father of the White Revolution** in India.
 
• He was the brain behind **Operation Flood**, which transformed India from a milk-deficient nation into the world’s largest milk producer.
 
• He founded the **National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)** and the brand **Amul**.
 
 
 
• **Norman Borlaug**:
 
 
• Recognized as the **Father of the Green Revolution** globally.
 
• An American biologist who won the **Nobel Peace Prize** in 1970 for developing semi-dwarf, high-yield, disease-resistant wheat varieties.
 
 
 
• **C. Subramaniam**:
 
 
• Served as the **Union Minister for Food and Agriculture** during the mid-1960s.
 
• He provided the critical **political leadership** and administrative framework that allowed the scientific advancements of the Green Revolution to be implemented successfully.
 
• He was awarded the **Bharat Ratna** in 1998.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the Subhadra Yojana?

options.text: Financial aid to economically weaker women

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Financial aid to economically weaker women**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Subhadra Yojana** is a landmark social welfare initiative launched by the **Government of Odisha** to promote **gender equality** and the **financial independence** of women in the state.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to provide **direct financial assistance** to women belonging to **economically weaker sections**, enabling them to meet their personal and entrepreneurial needs.
 
• The scheme targets approximately **1 crore women** across Odisha, focusing on those in the age group of **21 to 60 years** who do not fall under high-income brackets or government employment.
 
• Each eligible beneficiary receives a total financial benefit of **Rs. 50,000** over a period of **five years**, which is deposited directly into their **Aadhaar-linked bank accounts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Launch Details**:

 
 
• The scheme was officially launched by Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** on **September 17, 2024**, in **Bhubaneswar**, marking his 74th birthday.
 
• The initiative is part of the state government's commitment to fulfill its **election manifesto** regarding women's welfare.
 
 
 
• **Disbursement Mechanism**:
 
 
• The annual assistance of **Rs. 10,000** is paid in two equal installments of **Rs. 5,000** each.
 
• The first installment is typically released on **Rakhi Purnima** and the second on **International Women's Day** (March 8).
 
• The use of **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** and **Subhadra Cards** ensures transparency and prevents leakages in the system.
 
 
 
• **Exclusion Criteria**:
 
 
• To ensure the benefit reaches the most **vulnerable populations**, women from families paying **income tax**, or those receiving more than **Rs. 1,500 per month** from other government schemes, are generally excluded.

questions.question: The introduction of new crops such as sugarcane and improved irrigation under the Sultanate resulted in?
questions.solution:

questions.question: In the context of Earth Structure, which of the following discontinuity divides the crust and mantle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Moho**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mohorovicic discontinuity**, colloquially known as the **Moho**, is the boundary layer that separates the **Earth's crust** from the underlying **mantle**.
 
• It was identified in **1909** by **Andrija Mohorovicic**, a Croatian seismologist, who observed that **seismic waves** accelerated upon reaching this depth due to a change in rock density.
 
• The **Moho** lies at an average depth of **8 kilometers** beneath the ocean floor and roughly **32 to 70 kilometers** beneath **continental landmasses**, particularly under high mountain ranges.
 
• This transition represents a major chemical and rheological shift, moving from the **silica-rich** rocks of the crust to the **peridotite-rich** materials of the **upper mantle**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conrad Discontinuity**:

 
 
• It acts as the transition zone between the **upper continental crust** (granitic layer) and the **lower continental crust** (basaltic layer).
 
• It is not as globally persistent as the **Moho** and is primarily detected in **continental lithosphere**.
 
 
 
• **Repetti Discontinuity**:
 
 
• This boundary separates the **upper mantle** from the **lower mantle** (mesosphere).
 
• It is typically located at a depth of approximately **660 kilometers** and is characterized by phase changes in **silicate minerals**.
 
 
 
• **Gutenberg Discontinuity**:
 
 
• It defines the interface between the **mantle** and the **outer core**.
 
• Located at a depth of about **2,900 kilometers**, it marks the point where **S-waves** disappear and **P-waves** slow down significantly due to the liquid nature of the **outer core**.
 
 
 
• **Lehmann Discontinuity**:
 
 
• This is the boundary between the **liquid outer core** and the **solid inner core**.
 
• It occurs at a depth of about **5,150 kilometers** below the **Earth's surface**.

questions.question: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was also known by which of the following names?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Badshah Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan** was a towering figure in the **Indian independence movement** and a close associate of **Mahatma Gandhi**, known for his commitment to **non-violence**.
 
• He was affectionately called **Badshah Khan** (meaning 'King of Chiefs') by his followers in the **North-West Frontier Province (NWFP)**, reflecting his immense spiritual and political authority.
 
• He founded the **Khudai Khidmatgar** (Servants of God) in **1929**, a non-violent resistance group that played a pivotal role in the struggle against **British imperialism**.
 
• Due to his shared ideology and close friendship with Gandhi, he earned the title **Frontier Gandhi** (Sarhadi Gandhi) for leading the **Civil Disobedience Movement** in the frontier regions.
 
• In **1987**, he became the first non-Indian to be honored with the **Bharat Ratna**, India's highest civilian award, recognizing his lifelong dedication to **peace** and **human rights**.
 
• He was a vocal opponent of the **Partition of India**, championing the cause of a united India and later advocating for the rights of the **Pashtun** people.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baba-e-Qaum**:

 
 
• This title signifies **Father of the Nation**. It is primarily used to refer to **Muhammad Ali Jinnah** in Pakistan, while in India, **Mahatma Gandhi** is addressed as **Rashtrapita** or **Baba-e-Qaum**.
 
 
 
• **Raja ji**:
 
 
• This was the popular moniker for **Chakravarti Rajagopalachari**, an influential statesman, freedom fighter, and the last **Governor-General of India**.
 
 
 
• **Sardar**:
 
 
• This title, meaning **Chief** or **Leader**, was famously conferred upon **Vallabhbhai Patel** by the women of **Bardoli** following his successful leadership during the **Bardoli Satyagraha** of **1928**.

questions.question: _______ protects the crop from both frost and hot air currents.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Irrigation** is the process of supplying **water** to crops at regular intervals, which is vital for protecting them from extreme weather conditions like **frost** and **hot air currents**.
 
• **Water** has a high **specific heat capacity**, which allows it to absorb and store a large amount of **thermal energy** during the day and release it slowly at night, preventing the **soil temperature** from dropping to dangerous levels during **frost**.
 
• In the presence of **hot air currents** or **Loo**, water is absorbed by the roots and moves through the plant to the leaves, where it evaporates in a process called **transpiration**.
 
• The evaporation of water from the **stomata** creates a **cooling effect** on the plant surface, much like sweating in humans, which prevents the **protoplasm** from drying out and protects **plant tissues** from **desiccation**.
 
• Maintaining adequate **soil moisture** through **irrigation** ensures that the plant remains **turgid**, allowing it to withstand the physical stress caused by strong, dry winds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manure**

 
 
• It is an **organic substance** obtained from the decomposition of **plant or animal wastes** by microbes.
 
• It improves **soil texture** and **water-holding capacity** but does not directly provide **thermal insulation** against frost.
 
 
 
• **Fertilisers**
 
 
• These are **chemical substances** produced in factories that are rich in specific **nutrients** like **Nitrogen**, **Phosphorus**, and **Potassium**.
 
• Common examples include **Urea**, **Ammonium sulphate**, **Super phosphate**, and **NPK**.
 
 
 
• **Starch**
 
 
• A **carbohydrate** and **polysaccharide** that serves as the primary **energy storage** molecule in plants.
 
• It is synthesized during **photosynthesis** and stored in various organs like **roots**, **tubers**, and **seeds** for future metabolic use.

questions.question: As per the Global Remittances Inflow Report, India got ____ of global remittances in 2024.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14.3%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to recent data from the **World Bank** and global remittance monitors, **India** maintained its position as the top recipient of remittances worldwide in **2024**.
 
• India captured approximately **14.3%** of the total global remittance inflows, which underscores the significant economic footprint of the **Indian diaspora**.
 
• The total remittance value for **India** reached an estimated **$124 billion**, showing a growth of over **7%** compared to the previous year.
 
• This substantial share is attributed to the high concentration of **Indian migrants** in high-income countries like the **United States**, the **United Kingdom**, and the **United Arab Emirates**.
 
• Remittances into **India** currently represent nearly **3%** of the nation's **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**, serving as a critical source of foreign exchange and external financing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Remittance Trends**:

 
 
• In **2024**, total global remittance flows reached approximately **$860 billion**, with low- and middle-income countries receiving the bulk of these funds.
 
• Other leading recipients following **India** include **Mexico**, **China**, the **Philippines**, and **Egypt**.
 
• The **South Asia** region as a whole saw a growth in remittances, largely driven by the surge in inflows to **India**.
 
 
 
• **Key Drivers of Inflows**:
 
 
• **High-Skilled Migration**: There is an increasing shift toward high-skilled migration to **OECD** countries, which yields higher per-capita remittances.
 
• **Digital Integration**: The expansion of the **Unified Payments Interface (UPI)** for cross-border payments has reduced transaction costs and increased the speed of transfers.
 
• **GCC Contribution**: While the **United States** is the largest source, the **Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC)** countries continue to be a vital corridor for **India**.
